first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that reducing signup friction and shortening onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and early activation. This directly addresses both deteriorating metrics while better aligning with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, which carries a documented 30-day retention penalty. Verification should confirm durability, segment applicability, and downstream revenue quality before commitment.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying the self-serve SMB onboarding flow. The verified evidence directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and likely supports recovery of activation: shortened onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification raised activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%. Keep the test segment-specific because signup simplification was not replicated outside SMB, and monitor retention because that experiment showed a small 1% decline. Promotional pricing is not preferred despite competitive pressure because inherited evidence shows material retention harm.
